'''Alain E. Kaloyeros''' ({{langx|el|Αλεν Καλόγερος}}, {{langx|ar| آلان كالوييروس}}, born 1956, [[Beirut]])<ref name="timesunion.com1">{{cite web|url=http://www.timesunion.com/business/article/ALAIN-KALOYEROS-Nano-czar-studies-paranoia-679888.php|title=ALAIN KALOYEROS: Nano czar studies paranoia, crazy bosses|first=Paul|last=Grondahl|website=timesunion.com|publisher=[[Times Union (Albany)|Times Union]]|date=29 September 2010|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref> is an [[Americans|American]] [[physicist]]. He was the chief executive officer and sixth president of the [[SUNY Polytechnic Institute]] in [[Utica, New York]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alain E. Kaloyeros |url=http://www.sunycnse.com/AboutUs/FacultyStaff/ExecutiveStaff/AlainEKaloyeros.aspx |website=www.sunycnse.com |accessdate=2015-08-25 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823072352/http://www.sunycnse.com/aboutus/facultystaff/executivestaff/alainekaloyeros.aspx |archivedate=2015-08-23 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lohud.com/story/news/politics/politics-on-the-hudson/2016/02/11/new-bill-would-limit-kaloyeros-pay/80256304/|title=New bill would limit Kaloyeros' pay|publisher=[[lohud.com]]|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Kaloyeros was born in [[Beirut]] to a Lebanese mother and [[Greek people|Greek]] father.<ref name="uticaod.com"/> His family is [[Greek Orthodox]] Christian.<ref name="timesunion.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.timesunion.com/local/article/It-s-about-achievement-3690833.php|title='It's about achievement'|first=James M.|last=Odato|work=Times Union |publisher=timesunion.com|date=9 July 2012|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="uticaod.com"/> He attended [[Lebanese University]] and graduated with a License D’Enseignement in Mathematics and Physics with honors and left Lebanon in 1980 for graduate school in [[Florida]] at the [[University of Miami]], and he transferred to the [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name="timesunion.com1"/><ref name="timesunion.com"/> Kaloyeros graduated from The University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign with a doctorate in [[Experimental physics|Experimental]] [[Condensed matter physics|Condensed Matter Physics]] in 1987 with a perfect grade point average of 5.000/5.000.<ref name="albany.edu"/><ref name="nytimes.com"/><ref name="bloomberg.com"/><ref name="nytimes.com1">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/07/26/nyregion/public-lives-behind-a-research-center-a-geek-with-great-cars.html|title=Behind a Research Center, a Geek With Great Cars|first=Robin|last=Finn|date=26 July 2002|work=The New York Times|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/business/article/A-round-of-applause-for-CEG-2261194.php|title=A round of applause for CEG|first=Larry|last=Rulison|website=sfgate.com|publisher=|date=9 November 2011|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref>
Kaloyeros has authored and co-authored over 200 scientific articles in technical journals and contributed to 8 books on topics pertaining to the science and technology of nanotechnology, nanoelectronics, nano-optoelectronics, nano-medicine, and green energy. His technical focus was in ultrathin film materials and structures, atomic layer vapor phase deposition processes, and nanoscale x-ray, electron, and photon-based characterization and metrology. He advised more than 36 Ph.D. and over 100 Masters students. His work has been referenced in over 4,700 citations by his peers in scientific and technical publications.  He was awarded 14 U.S. and international patents.

==Career==
Kaloyeros was a professor in the [[University at Albany]]'s physics department from 1988 until 2009 when the nanotechnology research center was spun-off from the department into a separate SUNY college.<ref name="uticaod.com"/><ref name="bloomberg.com"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timesunion.com/local/article/Kaloyeros-rise-to-power-in-the-Capital-Region-9239017.php|title=Kaloyeros' rise to power in the Capital Region high-tech economy|first=Larry|last=Rulison|work=Times Union |publisher=timesunion.com|date=22 September 2016|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="timesunion.com"/> He was a Professor of [[Nanoscience]] at the [[SUNY Poly Colleges of Nanoscale Science and Engineering]] (CNSE) at [[University at Albany, SUNY]].<ref name="albany.edu"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/07/19/nyregion/albany-no-longer-a-secret-in-high-tech-chip-world.html|title=Albany No Longer a Secret In High-Tech Chip World|author=Richard Pérez-Peña|author-link=Richard Pérez-Peña|date=19 July 2002|work=The New York Times|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref>

In January 2015, he was appointed the sixth president of [[SUNY Polytechnic Institute]] (SUNY Poly).<ref name="uticaod.com"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/10/26/nyregion/cuomo-bets-on-solar-power-to-get-buffalo-on-its-feet.html|title=Despite Risks, Cuomo Bets on Solar Power to Lift Buffalo|author=Susanne Craig|author-link=Susanne Craig|date=26 October 2015|work=The New York Times|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref> He served as the Executive Director of the Center of Excellence in Nanoelectronics, the Interconnect Focus Center – New York, the Energy/Environment Technologies Applications Center, and the New York State Center for Advanced Thin Film Technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ecse.rpi.edu/Homepages/shur/Broadband/fac_kaloyeros.html|title=Researchers - Alain Kaloyeros|website=rpi.edu|publisher=Department of Electrical, Computer, and Systems Engineering, [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]]|accessdate=23 September 2016|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923114214/https://www.ecse.rpi.edu/Homepages/shur/Broadband/fac_kaloyeros.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/11/16/nyregion/hope-for-the-upstate-economy-in-the-next-wave-of-computer-chips.html|title=Hope for the Upstate Economy in the Next Wave of Computer Chips|author=James C. McKinley, Jr.|author-link=James C. McKinley, Jr.|date=16 November 2003|work=The New York Times|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref>

==Legal issues==
In September 2016, Kaloyeros was charged with felony [[bid rigging]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timesunion.com/local/article/Source-SUNY-Poly-s-Kaloyeros-developer-Niccola-9239293.php|title=Complaint charges SUNY Poly's Kaloyeros, developer Nicolla with bid-rigging|work=Times Union |date=22 September 2016 |publisher=timesunion.com|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="nytimes.com" /> He was then suspended from his job as SUNY Polytechnic Institute's President.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/albany/news/2016/09/22/suny-poly-president-alain-kaloyeros-suspended-from.html|title=SUNY Poly President Alain Kaloyeros suspended from job, Gov. Andrew Cuomo announces - Albany Business Review|publisher=bizjournals.com|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.timesunion.com/local/article/SUNY-suspends-Kaloyeros-without-pay-appoints-9239718.php|title=SUNY suspends Kaloyeros without pay, appoints system administrators to lead SUNY Poly|first=Bethany|last=Bump|work=Times Union |publisher=timesunion.com|date=22 September 2016|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chronicle.com/blogs/ticker/suny-polytechnic-president-charged-with-felony-bid-rigging-is-suspended-without-pay/114576|title=SUNY Polytechnic President, Charged With Felony Bid-Rigging, Is Suspended Without Pay – The Ticker - Blogs - The Chronicle of Higher Education|first=Fernanda|last= Zamudio-Suaréz|website=chronicle.com|publisher=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]|date=22 September 2016|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref>

On July 12, 2018, Kaloyeros was found guilty of wire fraud and conspiracy in a federal trial in Manhattan. The judge, [[Valerie E. Caproni]], scheduled the sentencing dates in October. The case is being appealed to the U.S. second circuit.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/07/12/nyregion/kaloyeros-guilty-buffalo-billion-cuomo.html|title=Architect of Cuomo's Buffalo Billion Project Is Convicted in Bid-Rigging Scheme|work=The New York Times |date=12 July 2018 |access-date=2018-07-13|language=en}}</ref> Following the verdict, the [[State University of New York]] announced that it would seek his removal from his tenured faculty position.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.suny.edu/suny-news/press-releases/july-2018/7-12-18-statement-kaloyeros-verdict/|title=7-12-18 Statement Kaloyeros Verdict - SUNY|last=SUNY|website=www.suny.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-07-13}}</ref>

After delays due to poor health, Kaloyeros began serving time in a federal prison in February 2022. He was released on July 2, 2022 (along with three other men - Joseph Geraldi, Steven Aiello and Louis Ciminelli) after serving about five months in prison.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.timesunion.com/education/article/Kaloyeros-out-of-prison-as-U-S-Supreme-Court-17287899.php | title=Kaloyeros out of prison as U.S. Supreme Court takes up appeal | date=6 July 2022 }}</ref>

On May 15, 2023, in a unanimous decision, the [[Supreme Court of the United States]] overturned Kaloyeros's conviction.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-12 |title=U.S. Supreme Court tosses Percoco, Kaloyeros convictions |url=https://www.news10.com/news/u-s-supreme-court-tosses-percoco-kaloyeros-convictions/ |access-date=2024-11-24 |website=NEWS10 ABC |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kaloyeros is married to Jessica Kaloyeros.
Kaloyeros is divorced from Paula Kaloyeros who he had two sons with, Nicholas and Alexander.<ref name="nytimes.com1"/><ref name="timesunion.com"/> He lives in [[Guilderland, New York]], a suburb of [[Albany, New York|Albany]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.syracuse.com/crime/index.ssf/2016/09/heads_of_suny_poly_and_albany_construction_company_charged_with_bid_rigging_1.html|title=Heads of SUNY Poly and Albany construction company charged with bid rigging|first=Rick|last=Moriarty|website=syracuse.com|publisher=[[The Post-Standard]]|date=22 September 2016|accessdate=23 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="timesunion.com1"/>
